chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Bebop sounded like 'scrambled eggs'
summary: He found Parker, Gillespie and Monk's music different but still real music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Okay. But what did you did think of the new music as a style, just in general? What did you think of this music that Charlie Parker was playing, and Dizzy Gillespie, and Bud Powell?

Well, to me, I didn't... I couldn't get it under my finger just what it was. But it was music, but it was a different style. I always recognized a tune, you might play a little melody once in a while. But if you didn't know what number that was playing, you wouldn't... You know. All of it sounded like scrambled eggs to me! Heh-heh.

But it was music, though. It had some foundation. Guys with good names, good musicians. This guy, a piano player, Thelonious Monk, all during that time Thelonious Monk. And Dizzy, Charlie Parker and other musicians I just can't remember right now. But you had a lot of them.
